slides.title: Everything is numbers
slides.text: Inside a computer, every number, letter and color is stored as bits: switches that are on (1) or off (0).
slides.alt: Five bits worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1: 16, 4 and 1 are on, so the bits read 10101 and the total is 21.

focus.cue: Letters are numbers too: A is 1
Bits on and off make a number

slides.title: Binary place values
slides.text: In binary each place is worth double the one to its right: 16, 8, 4, 2, 1. Switches 16, 4 and 1 on read 10101, which is 16 + 4 + 1 = 21.
slides.alt: Five bits worth 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1: 16, 4 and 1 are on, so the bits read 10101 and the total is 21.

slides.title: More bits, more values
slides.text: One bit shows 2 values. Each extra bit doubles that: 2 bits show 4, 3 bits show 8. Eight bits, a byte, show 256.
slides.alt: Eight bits make a byte, worth 128 down to 1. The 128 bit alone is on: a middle gray, 128.

focus.cue: The 128 bit on: a middle gray

slides.title: One thing, many codes
slides.text: The same data can be written many ways. Each way is an encoding. A color can be three numbers too: red 220, green 90, blue 40 is this orange.
slides.alt: Match the swatch: the target is 220, 90, 40, an orange. Red 220, green 100, blue 40 already looks the same.

focus.cue: Lots of red, some green, little blue: orange

words.means: one way of writing data as numbers
a color as three numbers: red, green and blue

slides.title: Gizmo's piece lights up
slides.text: Gizmo's piece flies home: four of four. The pieces are ready, but the Spark is not back yet. Unit 6 is about the people technology is for. Finish it, and you put the Spark together.

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Inside the Machine at Bits & Pixels and finish all 7 levels. Flip switches to send numbers, letters and gray levels.
